_comment: Illustrated site maps: AI-generated block dioramas (Higgsfield nano_banana_2) traced from Orrery's own reference maps of LROC / HiRISE imagery and the mission traverse data. Shown in the site panel's STORY tab (first card) and on /moon/<id> and /mars/<id>; listed on /colophon. validate-data checks that the file and its ladder rungs exist.

illustrations.title: Apollo 11
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC NAC imagery and the Apollo 11 landing-site data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Apollo 11 landing site at Tranquility Base: the Eagle lunar module stands in the centre, with the TV camera, the US flag, the seismometer and the retroreflector around it; Little West Crater and a double crater are labelled nearby.

illustrations.title: Apollo 12
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC NAC imagery and the Apollo 12 landing-site data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Apollo 12 landing site in the Ocean of Storms: the Intrepid lunar module, the US flag and the ALSEP station sit beside Surveyor crater, where the Surveyor 3 probe stands; Head, Bench and Block craters are labelled, and faint traverse tracks wind between them.

illustrations.title: Apollo 14
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC NAC imagery and the Apollo 14 landing-site data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Apollo 14 landing site at Fra Mauro: the Antares lunar module and the US flag, with the ALSEP science station a short walk away along a faint track and the Triplet Craters nearby.

illustrations.title: Apollo 15
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC imagery and the Apollo 15 traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Apollo 15 landing site beside Hadley Rille: in the centre are the Falcon lunar module, the ALSEP science station and the Lunar Rover; traverse routes lead to Station 1 (Elbow), Station 2 (St. George), Station 4 (Dune) and Station 7 (Spur).

illustrations.title: Apollo 16
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC imagery and the Apollo 16 traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Apollo 16 landing site in the Descartes Highlands: the Orion lunar module, the ALSEP station and the Lunar Rover stand at the centre between two bright ray craters; traverse routes lead to Station 1 (Plum), Station 4 (Stone Mountain) and Station 11 (North Ray Crater).

illustrations.title: Apollo 17
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC imagery and the Apollo 17 traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Apollo 17 landing site in the Taurus–Littrow valley: the Challenger lunar module, the ALSEP station and the Lunar Rover stand on the valley floor between the North Massif, the South Massif and the Sculptured Hills; traverse routes lead to Stations 1 to 9.

illustrations.title: Luna 17
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC imagery and the Lunokhod 1 traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Luna 17 landing site in Mare Imbrium: the Luna 17 lander stands at the centre, and the looping route of Lunokhod 1 passes a bright crater and ends at the rover’s last position.

illustrations.title: Luna 21
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC imagery and the Lunokhod 2 traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Luna 21 landing site in Le Monnier crater: the Luna 21 lander stands on the plain, and the route of Lunokhod 2 leads to the foot of a ridge and on to the rover’s last position, near the Fossa Recta rille.

illustrations.title: Chang’e 3
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC NAC imagery and the Yutu traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Chang’e 3 landing site in Mare Imbrium: the Chang’e 3 lander, the short looping route of the Yutu rover to its last position, and a large 450 m crater beside them.

illustrations.title: Chang’e 4
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC NAC imagery and the Yutu-2 traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Chang’e 4 landing site in Von Kármán crater: the Chang’e 4 lander stands in the east, the Yutu-2 position of May 2019 lies a short way west, and the rover’s route winds a long way west and north-west to its last position, marked by a small rover.

illustrations.title: Chandrayaan-3
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of LROC NAC imagery and the Pragyan traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of the Chandrayaan-3 landing site at Shiv Shakti Point: the Vikram lander and the winding route of the Pragyan rover to its last position, on heavily cratered terrain.

illustrations.title: Spirit
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of CTX imagery and the Spirit traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of Spirit’s route across Gusev Crater, 2004–2010: from the landing site (sol 0) past Bonneville Crater (sol 66), Columbia Hills (sol 159) and the Hills summit (sol 581) to Home Plate (sol 744) and the rover’s final position (sol 2210).

illustrations.title: Opportunity
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of CTX imagery and the Opportunity traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of Opportunity’s route across Meridiani Planum, 2004–2018: from Challenger Memorial Station (sol 0) past Eagle Crater (sol 56), Endurance Crater (sol 95), Erebus Crater (sol 652) and Victoria Crater (sol 952) to the Endeavour Crater rim (sol 2681), Marathon Valley (sol 4081) and the rover’s final position (sol 5111).

illustrations.title: Curiosity
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of HiRISE / CTX imagery and the Curiosity traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of Curiosity’s route across Gale Crater: from Bradbury Landing (sol 0) past the John Klein drill site (sol 182), Marias Pass (sol 992), Murray Buttes (sol 1451), Vera Rubin Ridge (sol 1805) and Greenheugh Pediment (sol 3413) to the rover’s position at sol 5045, with the way on to Mount Sharp.

illustrations.title: Perseverance
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of CTX imagery and the Perseverance traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of Perseverance’s route across Jezero Crater since 2021: from the landing site (sol 0) past Ingenuity’s Flight 1 (sol 58), the first core (sol 190), Hawksbill Gap (sol 440), Three Forks Depot (sol 653) and the Margin unit (sol 915) to the rover’s position on sol 2022.

illustrations.title: Zhurong
illustrations.made_from: Orrery reference map of CTX imagery and the Zhurong traverse data
illustrations.alt: Illustrated block map of Zhurong’s route across Utopia Planitia, 2021–2022: from the landing platform (sol 0) past the sol 60 marker and 100 days on Mars (sol 97) to the rover’s final position (sol 347).
